title: TV parses phone input packets from the frame bytes (no JSON tree, regex or CharBuffer)
body:
## Summary
Each 30-60 Hz input packet allocated ~30 KB on the TV before reaching the mailbox; now ~5 KB.

## Description
RaceServer.handle ran frame.readText() (ktor allocates a CharBuffer) then Json.parseToJsonElement and ten JsonPrimitive.doubleOrNull reads, each of which runs a kotlin Regex (Matcher + int[]). New InputPacket reads the ByteArray in place with a Clinger fast path for numbers and falls back to the old path on anything unusual.

## Flow
frame.data -> InputPacket.parse -> handleInput (offer, metrics, ack from a reused StringBuilder). Unknown shapes, quoted numbers, escapes, fragmented frames -> old JSON path unchanged.

## Expected impact
Less young-gen garbage and CPU on the Ktor thread at 2 phones x 60 pkt/s on the Stick's weak cores (GC pauses compete with the render thread).

## Evaluation
Claim: Per-packet host allocation drops by >70% with identical accept/reject behaviour.
Before: 31.7 KB/packet (v0: 29.7 KB without the later JSON-path tweaks), parse 7.8 KB / 3.3 us
After: 5.6-7.7 KB/packet; compact packet parse 15 B / 0.09-0.24 us
Method: LinkBenchTest (real socket, 3000 packets at 300/s, server-thread ThreadMXBean bytes, assertions off) and ParseBenchTest; InputPacketTest compares 20k random + 50k mutated packets with the JSON tree.
Result: better
Gate: gradlew :link:test green (incl. InputPacketTest/HudPayloadTest/PackedTest); probe.mjs and browser-check.mjs green against FakeHost

title: TV stops resending an unchanged hud snapshot (1 s heartbeat) and writes it with fixed-point numbers
body:
## Summary
A phone in a menu received 10 identical 1 KB frames a second; now one.

## Description
hudJob built and sent the full hud JSON every 100 ms. It now builds into two reused StringBuilders, compares with the last sent snapshot and sends only on change or after 1 s. Speed/drift numbers use appendFixed (2-3 decimals, no Double.toString).

## Flow
tick -> metadata.json -> build -> sameChars(last) -> send or skip.

## Expected impact
Idle downlink and per-frame TV work (encode, write) fall ~90% in lobby/garage/career/results/paused.

## Evaluation
Claim: Static state -> 1 frame/s; a change reaches the phone within one tick.
Before: 92 frames and 9.3 KB/s per 10 s per phone (idle)
After: 12 frames, 3.5 KB/s (then 0.62 KB/s with the refresh change)
Method: LinkBenchTest hud-static; HudPayloadTest asserts 2-5 frames in 3 s and that a speed change arrives within 500 ms.
Result: better
Gate: gradlew :link:test green (incl. InputPacketTest/HudPayloadTest/PackedTest); probe.mjs and browser-check.mjs green against FakeHost

title: Hud metadata (garage/career/car/track/feel) refresh 5 s -> 60 s
body:
## Summary
The reliable, ordered socket never loses a delta, yet every 5 s each phone got and re-rendered ~15 KB of metadata.

## Description
HudMetadata forced a full snapshot every 5000 ms. Now 60000 ms as a safety net; phase change and (re)connect still send everything.

## Flow
HudMetadata.json -> full when phase changes / first / 60 s.

## Expected impact
Removes a 15 KB parse + JSON.stringify compare + DOM rebuild hitch every 5 s on the phone and 3 KB/s of downlink.

## Evaluation
Claim: Idle 9.3 -> 0.62 KB/s, racing 9.46 -> 6.42 KB/s per phone.
Before: 9.3 / 9.46 KB/s
After: 0.62 / 6.42 KB/s
Method: LinkBenchTest with a 15 KB metadata fixture; HudMetadataTest updated.
Result: better
Gate: gradlew :link:test green (incl. InputPacketTest/HudPayloadTest/PackedTest); probe.mjs and browser-check.mjs green against FakeHost

title: Phone page writes DOM only when a value changed (ack and hud paths)
body:
## Summary
The controller dirtied layout 30 times a second while idle.

## Description
status() rewrote text and body classes on every ack (30-60/s); the RTT label was rewritten per ack; hud rewrote ~20 text nodes, rebuilt car stats and re-stringified garage/career for a deep compare 10x/s. Values are now cached; car/track/feel/garage/career are skipped by identity (hud delta keeps the objects); pause status no longer flickers against acks.

## Flow
ack/hud -> setText/setMeter/setClass/setAria (cache) -> DOM only on change.

## Expected impact
Less main-thread and battery on the phone, fewer dropped touch frames while driving.

## Evaluation
Claim: Lobby idle layouts/s 31 -> 0 and task ms/s 18.8 -> 5.7 (1x CPU).
Before: lobby: 31 layouts/s, 91 mutations/s, 18.8 ms/s; driving: 46 layouts/s, 484 mutations/s, 41.8 ms/s
After: lobby: 0 / 0 / 5.7; driving: 4.7 / 84 / 25.2 (4x CPU lobby 71 -> 10.5 ms/s)
Method: tools/controller-bench.mjs (Chrome, FakeHost, CDP Performance metrics + MutationObserver).
Result: better
Gate: browser-check.mjs and probe.mjs green; garage and career sheets render (Playwright screenshot, 0 page errors)

title: Minimal uplink input packet
body:
## Summary
Input packet carried 17-digit doubles and six zero fields (~105-141 B).

## Description
send() now builds the string directly: axes rounded to 0.001, ts to 0.1 ms, h/f/fire/mine/weapon/ability only when non-zero (host reads missing as 0). The 60 pkt/s cap (sendSoft 16 ms) re-verified: 250 Hz of pointermoves -> 62 pkt/s.

## Flow
send -> inputPacket -> ws.send.

## Expected impact
Less radio payload, and the TV parser stays on the zero-alloc fast path (17-digit doubles took a 1.4 KB slow path).

## Evaluation
Claim: Packet bytes -56..-60%.
Before: 105 B idle (3322 B/s), 141 B driving (7950 B/s)
After: 46 B idle (1475 B/s), 56 B driving (3125 B/s)
Method: controller-bench sentBytesPerS; ParseBenchTest 1353 B -> 15 B per parse.
Result: better
Gate: browser-check.mjs (incl. 62 pkt/s cap), probe.mjs green

title: Phone reconnect backoff and no retry while hidden
body:
## Summary
With the TV off the page opened a socket every 0.8 s forever.

## Description
onclose retried at a fixed 800 ms. Now 0.8, 1.6, then every 3.2 s, reset on welcome; nothing is scheduled while the page is hidden (visibilitychange already reconnects).

## Flow
onclose -> backoff timer -> connect.

## Expected impact
Battery and Wi-Fi wakeups when the TV is off or asleep; worst recovery +3.2 s.

## Evaluation
Claim: Attempts per minute 53 -> 20.
Before: 53/min (gaps 0.8 s)
After: 20/min (gaps 1.6, 3.2 s)
Method: tools/reconnect-bench.mjs (host process killed, 40 s window).
Result: better
Gate: browser-check.mjs green

title: Menu heartbeat 4 Hz instead of 30 Hz outside countdown/race
body:
## Summary
A phone sitting in a menu sent 30 inputs/s and received 30 acks/s although the host consumes input only in a race.

## Description
retime() switches the heartbeat interval: 33 ms in countdown/race or while any control is held, else 250 ms; ack-loss threshold 250 ms hot / 1.5 s idle with a grace on the switch. Edges still send immediately.

## Flow
hud.phase / pointer state -> retime -> setInterval period.

## Expected impact
Largest battery and TV-side saving for the long menu/garage/career sessions; TV ack work 2 x 30/s -> 2 x 4/s when both phones idle.

## Evaluation
Claim: Idle uplink 31.7 -> 5.4 pkt/s, main thread 6.2 -> 1.0 ms/s.
Before: 31.7 pkt/s, 1475 B/s, 6.2 ms/s
After: 5.4 pkt/s (incl. 1 Hz ping), 242 B/s, 1.0 ms/s
Method: controller-bench lobbyIdle/garageOpenIdle at 1x CPU.
Result: better
Gate: browser-check.mjs green (held-control freshness unchanged)

title: Controller page, hud.css and catalog served gzipped with ETag
body:
## Summary
74 KB went out raw on every load/reload; hud.css was re-read and the 26 KB catalog rebuilt per request.

## Description
Packed(text) holds UTF-8 and lazy gzip; respondPacked honours Accept-Encoding, adds ETag and no-cache for css/catalog, returns 304 on If-None-Match; clients without gzip get the old bytes.

## Flow
GET -> respondPacked -> gzip/raw/304.

## Expected impact
Faster first paint on weak Wi-Fi, less TV work per page load, free reloads after a TV restart.

## Evaluation
Claim: Page+css transfer -64%; linked in 373 -> 311 ms at 5 Mbit/s + 20 ms.
Before: 49.1 KB (page+css), catalog 25.8 KB, linked 373 ms
After: 17.6 KB, catalog 4.6 KB gzip, linked 311 ms
Method: controller-bench NET_MBPS=5 (CDP network emulation), curl gzip sizes; PackedTest.
Result: better
Gate: gradlew :link:test green (incl. InputPacketTest/HudPayloadTest/PackedTest); probe.mjs and browser-check.mjs green against FakeHost

title: Repeatable link instruments: FakeHost, controller-bench, benches; browser-check was red on deathride/main
body:
## Summary
The desktop host does not compile on the tip (WheelShots.kt), so no check could run; browser-check also failed on stale steer thresholds.

## Description
FakeHost = real RaceServer + real page + 60 Hz stand-in loop with a real-sized fixture; controller-bench reports CPU/layout/mutations/bytes per phase; LinkBenchTest/ParseBenchTest are opt-in (LINK_BENCH=1, LINK_JFR). browser-check thresholds assumed the doubled pad travel af448554 reverted (30 px = 0.32 of 95 px).

## Flow
gradlew -q :link:printTestClasspath; java -cp ... FakeHostKt controller tools/bench/hud-fixture.json; node tools/probe.mjs / browser-check.mjs / controller-bench.mjs.

## Expected impact
Future link work can be measured without a Stick or the desktop build. Also measured and left alone: Distribution.add 12 ns, Distribution.json 27 us, /stats 49 us / 156 KB (10 s log and probes only).

## Evaluation
Claim: Checks run and pass on the tip.
Before: browser-check red at 'diagonal combines steer + GO'
After: green
Method: Run against FakeHost; thresholds .4 -> .3 and .3 -> .15.
Result: better
Gate: browser-check.mjs, probe.mjs green

title: Link threads at lower priority than the render thread (Stick A/B)
body:
## Summary
Ktor/IO threads run at normal priority and share 4 cores with the GL thread.

## Description
Give the link scope and the CIO call dispatcher a daemon pool with Thread.MIN_PRIORITY+1 (ART maps this to a positive nice value), or a limitedParallelism(2) dispatcher; verify that CIO honours the supplied context.

## Flow
RaceServer scope/engine config -> custom ThreadFactory.

## Expected impact
Frame p95 on the Stick if input bursts or GC currently steal render time.

## Evaluation
Claim: Frame p95/worst improves or stays equal with two phones at 60 pkt/s.
Before: Stick p95 20-22 ms, worst 37-55 ms (brief)
After: 5e380025 (2026-10-06): link and Ktor workers at NORM_PRIORITY-2 (nice 13 on the Stick). P11 atrace, 29 frames over 33 ms in two 20 s captures: link threads took 0 ms of the render thread's 321.7 ms of preempted time, though they ran 29.8% of a core over the 900 s soak.
Method: A/B on the Stick with --soak and two probes (desktop cannot show it: Windows priority mapping differs).
Result: better - built in 5e380025; link threads no longer preempt the render thread (P11 trace)
Gate: needs a Stick

title: Replace ktor DefaultWebSocketSession with webSocketRaw on the hot socket
body:
## Summary
About 5 KB of the remaining per-packet host allocation is ktor internal (eager Frame.toString trace strings in runIncomingProcessor, ack encode).

## Description
webSocketRaw skips the default session's incoming processor; ping/pong/close must then be handled by hand (phone already sends its own 1 Hz ping).

## Flow
route /ws -> raw session -> same handle().

## Expected impact
A further ~30-50% off per-packet allocation.

## Evaluation
Claim: Per-packet alloc < 3 KB with close handshakes intact.
Before: 5.4 KB/packet
After: unmeasured
Method: LinkBenchTest inputs phase; CompactLinkTest and LinkTest for close/reconnect semantics.
Result: pending
Gate: needs spike; risk of close-handshake regressions

title: Trim the combat JSON in the racing hud (592 of ~700 chars)
body:
## Summary
The racing hud payload is mostly the per-tick combat object, with static strings (ability id/name, weaponName) repeated 10x/s.

## Description
combatJson is built in game/RaceGame (other stream). Send static fields only on change (like HudMetadata) or move them into the metadata block; the phone merges.

## Flow
game combatJson -> RaceServer slot -> hud.

## Expected impact
About 40% off racing downlink and phone parse.

## Evaluation
Claim: Racing hud 706 -> ~400 chars.
Before: 706 chars at 10 Hz
After: unmeasured
Method: LinkBenchTest hud-live with the split.
Result: pending
Gate: outside link write set

title: Tell the TV when the phone page is hidden and pause its hud
body:
## Summary
A locked or backgrounded phone keeps receiving 1-10 hud frames a second until the OS kills the socket.

## Description
Phone sends {t:'vis',v:0/1} on visibilitychange; RaceServer skips hud (not acks) while hidden and resumes with a full snapshot.

## Flow
visibilitychange -> raw -> slot.hidden -> hudJob.

## Expected impact
Downlink and phone wakeups while the screen is off.

## Evaluation
Claim: Hidden phone receives 0 hud frames.
Before: unmeasured
After: unmeasured
Method: Playwright page.evaluate to dispatch visibilitychange; count frames.
Result: pending
Gate: needs protocol addition on both sides

title: Thin accepted acks and idle race heartbeat
body:
## Summary
In a race each input is acked (2 x 60 frames/s at the TV, ~2.7 KB ktor garbage each) and a held, unchanged control still sends at 30 Hz.

## Description
Ack at most every 33 ms unless rejected; phone RTT/lastAck logic already tolerates it; unchanged state could drop to 15 Hz if Wi-Fi jitter evidence allows (stale limit 250 ms).

## Flow
handleInput ack gate; phone tick.

## Expected impact
Roughly halves TV ack work in a race.

## Evaluation
Claim: Acks/s 60 -> 30 per phone.
Before: 60 acks/s
After: unmeasured
Method: LinkBenchTest; CompactLinkTest currently expects an ack per input (needs updating).
Result: pending
Gate: existing test encodes per-input acks; needs on-device jitter data for the 15 Hz part

title: Phone micro-costs: cache the pad rect, rAF the pad visuals, ring-buffer the sent map, fast-path ack parsing
body:
## Summary
Remaining driving cost is small: 20.9 ms/s main thread at 1x, 4.7 layouts/s, 84 mutations/s; Classic layout 25.8 layouts/s from getBoundingClientRect after a left-style write.

## Description
steer() reads getBoundingClientRect per move; visuals and aria-valuenow are written per pointermove (up to 125/s); sent is a Map pruned at 120; every ack goes through JSON.parse.

## Flow
pointerdown caches rect; rAF applies visuals; Int32Array ring by q; ack prefix check.

## Expected impact
About 10-20% of the remaining ~21 ms/s while driving.

## Evaluation
Claim: Driving task ms/s 20.9 -> ~17.
Before: 20.9 ms/s (Drive), 34.1 ms/s (Classic)
After: unmeasured
Method: controller-bench raceDriving with BENCH_QUERY=&layout=Classic.
Result: pending
Gate: below the noise floor of one run

title: Per-slot uplink flood guard (about 120 packets/s)
body:
## Summary
A buggy or hostile client can send unbounded input frames; each costs ~5 KB of TV garbage.

## Description
Drop or close above 120 frames/s per connection over a 1 s window (the phone's cap is 62/s plus edges).

## Flow
handle loop counter.

## Expected impact
Bounds the worst-case CPU a stranger on the Wi-Fi can take once the PIN is known.

## Evaluation
Claim: Flood of 5000 pkt/s costs <= 120 pkt/s of work.
Before: unbounded
After: unmeasured
Method: LinkTest with a flood client.
Result: pending
Gate: needs policy decision on close vs drop

title: Serve /stats gzipped and build it in place (the probe's reader-side load on the Stick)
body:
## Summary
The probe reads the 77.5 KB /stats in a loop with a 160 ms pause. On the Stick that is most of the process's 7.7-7.8 MB/s allocation (109-111 GCs per 342 s), link-thread CPU, and Wi-Fi traffic whose data-usage alert re-polls NetworkStats (0.56-0.73 s of a core every ~7 s; 6 of 12 and 4 of 17 traced frames over 33 ms fell inside a poll).

## Description
cc882e7f: /stats and /profile gzipped (BEST_SPEED) when the request accepts it; statsJson appended into one reused buffer instead of Kotlin templates; Distribution.json sorts in a reused scratch array. StatsJsonTest: byte-identical text against the verbatim old code on a populated 77 KB state.

## Flow
probe GET /stats -> RaceServer.statsJson -> respondJsonText

## Expected impact
Fewer GCs and NetworkStats polls during the I2 probe arm; players' phones never read /stats.

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - fewer active frames over 33 ms and a lower worst-window p95
Before: deathride/main, two profiled 360 s runs: worst active p95 23.078 / 24.102 ms, over 33 ms 81 / 97, allocation 7.79 / 7.71 MB/s, PSS max 173.7 / 179.2 MiB
After: cut, two runs: worst active p95 26.965 / 22.335 ms, over 33 ms 44 / 49, active max 141.930 / 67.739 ms, allocation 3.51 / 3.47 MB/s, GCs 111/109 -> 49/49, PSS max 192.0 / 196.9 MiB, both at the first sample after the /routes warm-up; the uncut 900 s soak read 202.0 MiB at that same sample, so PSS does not separate the arms. NetworkStats CPU 8.6% (uncut soak) -> 2.8-2.9% of a core; Wi-Fi sent 472 -> 155-157 KB/s
Method: probe - perf-device --profile, 360 s, tools/perf-p11.py and perf-p11-compare.py (keep rule fixed before the cut ran: each cut run beats both baselines on worst p95 and on over-33 ms frames)
Result: not-better - reverted in e11edc7d: run 1's worst window (26.965 ms) was worse than both baselines. Over-33 ms frames -40% to -55% and allocation -55% are recorded for the operator; a longer A/B (more runs or a 900 s soak per arm) would settle it
Gate: StatsJsonTest (byte-identical text); the keep rule in tools/perf-p11-compare.py
